posts.cooked:
Mostly, SOTM is awesome.  Mostly.  But every once in a while, things line up in such a way as to make the game a cakewalk, a foregone conclusion, a frustrating grind, or just a pointless waste of effort.  This is obviously not optimal, and so I think we should brainstorm corrective measures.

Here are two examples from my experience of games that went to an unsatisfying place fast.

1.  My first battle against The Dreamer; I had taken five heroes, not knowing this would make her meaner, and within about four rounds all of my heroes had been completely destroyed, except for Fanatic (it might have been Aegis that saved her, I'm not sure; the game also included Haka, O-X, AZ and Tempest, so her HP was pretty much in the middle).  But turn 1 End of Days had wiped out the initial Projections, leading to the quick flip, and once there were enough new Projections out and they'd butchered Tempest, he used his incap ability to give Fanatic back End of Days.  That one card pretty much single-handedly nerfed what was otherwise an overwhelming force; under other circumstances, EoD pulling out a last-second win against overwhelming odds might be awesome, but without the need to kill an actual villain after the minions were defeated, it was just too pathetic, and I've sworn never to use Fanny against Dreamy again (unless I just get really sick of losing to her).

2.  In one particular game where I was introducing a new player to the game, I was bored with the standard "newbie" villains like Baron Blade, Omnitron and arguably Plague Rat, and tried one other who I regarded as fairly easy: Spite.  However, my friend who usually plays Fanatic was trying out Visionary that week, and he opened on 2x Twist the Ether, putting both on Spite, and that was pretty much game; once he flipped, Spite could never deal any damage at all due to the low H value, except for 1 point getting through whenever we used a Power thanks to Compound Xi.  So he just stood there while we took him apart bit by bit.  I've also seen pre-flip Spite neutered for several full turns by having one member of the party tank while immune to damage; Nightmist can do this, as can Visionary, and a Scholar with multiple Flesh to Irons could even do it while retaining the ability to play cards.  Since turning off his damage also turns off his healing, non-advanced Spite is a pushover with such a tank in the party, and even his advanced version is beatable...while under other circumstances, that advanced healing means you might as well not even try damaging him until he flips (unless your damage output is truly spectacular).  Either way, such a sense of pointlessness is something we should try to avoid in our games.

Example 2 has rather led me to the conclusion that Spite is really not a very well-designed villain deck, compared to most of the others, and tends to lead me to not want to play him very often.  The Agent of Gloom of course helps considerably by offering an alternative, but he's still saddled with a villain deck where a lot of the card plays are blank and almost none of them are highly consequential.  I find myself wondering how the general concept of "transhuman serial killer" could be better executed....the very same set that contained Spite also contained the Chairman and the Matriarch, with all of them being highly experimental designs for bringing an unorthodox battle scenario to life, and the other two worked brilliantly.  Two out of three ain't bad, I suppose, but I still feel like it'd be nice to be able to "fix" Spite, and similar adjustments could be made to other lacking villains, such as Ambuscade and Kismet.

(We could kind of overlap here with the Playtesting Nostalgia thread, if anyone here has been around for so long that they remember the process of getting Spite, Chair and Matty to their current states.  It's entirely possible that Spite was just as much of a beast as the other two at one point in his design, and I'm curious whether that changed, and if so why the others were allowed to remain as fearsome as they are, while he was nerfed so significantly.)

I'm strongly inclined to suspect that >G chose Spite to get a promo because he was kinda lame…or perhaps he was intentionally made kinda lame because they intended to give him a promo later.  Same for Gloomweaver, except there he's not lame so much as just weak (although I do think Gloomy is lame in one sense…he almost never flips, and yet when he does flip, it's not that big a deal); they probably intentionally made him underwhelming at first, so that they could do the Skinweaver thing later and be more impressive.

my problem with modifying Spite is that his flavour is really good, his mechanics are the ones lacking a bit.

The mechanics were what I had in mind to change.  Perhaps instead of just automatically getting a second card play each turn, all Victims ought to give him a play, so that he'd always do something relevant on his turn.  And his Advanced text on side 1 definitely needs to change.  Then on Side 2, he's a complete robot, and deals only 2-damage instances which are too easy to shut down.  I'd have him maybe reveal a card, and do one of three things depending on whether it's a Victim, a one-shot, or Collateral Damage.  Also he needs to have some way of dealing with Ongoing or Environment cards, which can shut him down too completely otherwise.

So if this OT is ok, I'll continue a bit here. Afterall variants is what I most talk about in thsese forums. Thing is, in this game mechanics are tightly related to theme. For example, Spite flipping when 5 drugs cards are out  strongly represents him flipping out, so changing that mechanic changes that part of the theme. I feel he should feel like a race between saving victims and delaying drugs, that once he is turned into his monster side you have to finish him off fast or he'll overrun you eventually.

I think I could try this... changing his healing on his first side to: "The first time Spite deals damage..." so there's not THAT much healing on his first side (basically just H-1 from his card and not also from all the Victims and drugs) and changing his monster side to "Whenever a Villain Card would be played, instead put it under this card. Spite deals the Hero Target with the lowest HP X projectile damage, where X is the number of cards below this card". That forces you to take action early and dispatch him fast once he flipped.

About Plage Rat: every Villian has some case where they are a dud. I think it's perfect he doesn't do stuff with the Environment, he is a Rat.

Plague Rat is another villain I'd like to see adjusted to remove his glaringly obvious weaknesses.  I love how hyper-violent he is, but very early in my time playing the game, I read a game report about him on Mars where Meteor Storm came out, and he couldn't remove it, so the heroes just ignored him while they built up to OHK him after finally removing it.  That is a lame game, though PR is generally not lame otherwise.  But if he was up against Visionary, Nightmist and Scholar, lameness could definitely occur as he's just incapable of getting any damage through and Infections don't actually do anything.  (Heck, Scholar would be able to use PR's flipside ability to bite his comrades harmlessly and regain HP.)  This is bordering on comical rather than lame, but still mostly that.

Yeah they definitely could have done more with the Infection status.  A really cool idea, and I'm sure they didn't want to dive in too deep with their first expansions, but I have a feeling if they remade Plague Rat today they could make the mechanic much more intricate.

The problem I have with Plague Rat is that he almost never flips (much like Gloomy).  He really has nothing in his deck but Infection cards and pure damage (that usually get out Infection cards faster), so if you find a way to gimp his damage and have plenty of Ongoing destruction, he is laughable (and even if he manages to flip, he won't stay flipped for more than a turn).

Just last night I did a round against PR with Haka, Visionary, OmniX, and Fanatic.  Haka and Fanatic completely shut down his damage output (Oh Ground Pound, you sexy beast) while Visionary and OmniX whacked the Infection cards as soon as they came out.

Sure he does H damage when you destroy an Infection, but Visionary always had a Projection out, OmniX had his Toxic reduction plating, and Haka/Fanatic can take the damage.

I'm sure there are some team setups that have more trouble, but overall, once you know what he has in his deck, controlling him is far too easy.
